::: {#rem-entropy-expected-surprisal}
#### Entropy is expected surprisal

The [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy)
of a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$ is the
[expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation)
of its [surprisal](#def-surprisal):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\entropyf{X}
&= \E{-\log \P(X)} \\
&= \E{\surprisalf{X}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

So $\entropyf{X}$ is the average number of [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) (with base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm))
needed to record a value of $X$
when each value $x$ costs $\surprisalf{x}$ bits.
The [source coding theorem](source-coding.qmd#thm-source-coding),
on a later page of these notes, makes that average precise:
no [uniquely decodable code](source-coding.qmd#def-uniquely-decodable) does better.

:::
